clue.text: Standard period over which environmental warming occurs

definitions.text: Standard period over which environmental warming occurs

parts.words: Standard period over which environmental warming occurs
parts.note: the clockwise standard adopted in warmer months (as in British daylight saving) is also simply the season when the weather heats up

explanation.surface: A climate-science line about the time span over which global warming takes place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Environmental warming' suggests climate change, but it is just the hot season; 'Standard period' points to the officially set clock time used in that season, like British Summer Time.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names both the warm season of the year and the adjusted clock standard observed during it.

clue.text: Bird family group returns to island

indicators.note: returns means the word for the family group is read backwards

parts.note: sib is a word for a sibling or kin group

explanation.surface: A flock of birds of one family flying back to an island home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'family group' is a short word for siblings; 'returns' flips it.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-billed wading bird, sacred in ancient Egypt, is one particular kind of bird.

clue.text: One's taken in by mostly routine philosopher

indicators.note: taken in by means the piece for one sits inside the other piece
mostly means the last letter of the routine word is dropped

parts.note: stock, as in a stock response, means routine or standard
one is I, the Roman numeral; the 's is 'is', a link

explanation.surface: Someone absorbed into a mostly dull, routine sort of thinker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts STOCK to STOC, and 'taken in by' puts I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A Stoic is a follower of the Greek school of Zeno, a classical philosophical tradition.

clue.text: God nearly shut up dwarf in Wagner stage show

parts.note: Pan is the Greek god of the wild
a door pulled to is pushed into the nearly closed position, so 'to' means nearly shut
Mime is the dwarf, brother of Alberich, in Wagner's Ring cycle

explanation.surface: A Wagner opera production in which a god half-imprisons a dwarf.
explanation.walkthrough: As in 'push the door to', TO describes a door brought nearly or fully closed.
explanation.definitionFit: A pantomime is a traditional British Christmas theatre entertainment, a kind of stage show.

clue.text: Mother parrot close to attack? Keep going

parts.note: ma is a familiar word for mother
the kea is a New Zealand parrot
nigh means near or close
a fit is a sudden attack, as of coughing

explanation.surface: Mother's parrot, near the moment of attack, is urged to carry on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'close' is the adjective meaning near, not the verb to shut.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to carry on celebrating or partying through the evening rather than stopping.

clue.text: No one with faith involved in robbery

parts.note: at means engaged in, as in 'at work'
a heist is a robbery

explanation.surface: A faithless person is caught up in a robbery.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who denies the existence of God has no religious belief at all.

clue.text: Concern with pilots having to work regular routes

definitions.text: Concern with pilots having to work regular routes

parts.words: Concern with pilots having to work regular routes
parts.note: a concern here is a business, one employing flyers who operate scheduled services

explanation.surface: Worry among pilots about being made to fly the same routes repeatedly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Concern' looks like worry, but it means a business firm.
explanation.definitionFit: A company operating scheduled air services employs pilots to fly fixed routes.

clue.text: Cut bad writer was taken back

parts.note: a hack is a poor, jobbing writer

indicators.note: taken back means the word was is read backwards

explanation.surface: A poor writer's work was cut and withdrawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken back' turns WAS into SAW.
explanation.definitionFit: The fine-toothed saw for metal can be used as a verb meaning to cut with one.

clue.text: A lot of pressure backing a fine stone pub

indicators.note: backing means the pieces for 'a fine stone' are read in reverse

parts.note: a gem is a fine or precious stone
a bar is a pub

explanation.surface: Pressure to support a pub built of fine stone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns AGEM into MEGA.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit of a million bars of pressure is a very large amount of it.

clue.text: Limit copulating freely? Not good for increasing numbers

indicators.note: freely means the remaining letters are rearranged at will
not means the letter for good is dropped from the fodder

explanation.surface: A cheeky call to restrict promiscuity, since breeding increases numbers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not good' removes G from LIMIT COPULATING; 'freely' rearranges the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Multiplying is the arithmetic operation that increases a number by repeated addition.

clue.text: Felt a hero in large body of soldiers

parts.note: a batt is a sheet of felted wadding
a lion is a brave, celebrated person

explanation.surface: A hero who felt at home in a large army unit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Felt' is not the verb but a noun: BATT, a sheet of matted fibre.
explanation.definitionFit: A battalion is an army unit of several companies, a large body of troops.

clue.text: English monarch dismissing Republican mathematician

indicators.note: dismissing means the letter for Republican is removed

parts.note: a ruler is a monarch

explanation.surface: An English king sends away a republican.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dismissing' takes R out of RULER, leaving ULER.
explanation.definitionFit: Leonhard Euler was the great eighteenth-century Swiss mathematician.

clue.text: Simple banning talk from illicit drinking den

indicators.note: banning means the word for talk is removed

parts.note: a speakeasy was a Prohibition-era illegal bar
speak means talk

explanation.surface: A plain rule against chatter in an illegal bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banning' removes SPEAK from SPEAKEASY.
explanation.definitionFit: Something easy is straightforward to do, needing no effort.

clue.text: Sixty hearts cut into middle of oak?

indicators.note: cut into means the hearts letter is carved inside the other piece

parts.note: an oak is one kind of tree, so its middle can be a tree's core; the question mark flags the example
H is the card-suit abbreviation for hearts

explanation.surface: Sixty love hearts carved into the heart of an oak.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'middle of oak' as TREE'S CORE and put H inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A score is twenty, so three of them make sixty, the old biblical count.

clue.text: Small tree used to make window frame

parts.note: the ash is a tree

explanation.surface: Wood from a small tree goes to make a window frame.
explanation.definitionFit: A sash is the sliding frame holding the glass in a sash window.

clue.text: My old walk initially is consequence of muscle disease

parts.note: a path is a walk

indicators.note: initially means the first letters of 'is' and 'consequence' are taken

explanation.surface: My old stroll suffers as a result of a muscular ailment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' covers both 'is' and 'consequence', giving IC.
explanation.definitionFit: Myopathy is any disease of muscle tissue; the adjectival form describes that condition.

clue.text: Clubs invested in St Cecilia ales brewed in the church

indicators.note: invested in means the clubs letter is put inside the rearranged letters
brewed means the letters of the saint and ales are stirred up

parts.note: C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs

explanation.surface: Clubs put money into ales brewed at St Cecilia's church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brewed' rearranges STCECILIAALES, and 'invested in' adds C inside them.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes matters belonging to clergy and church affairs.

clue.text: Hairstyle that's first rate for sailors

parts.note: top means first or best, as in top marks
a knot is a nautical unit of speed

explanation.surface: A hairdo that suits sailors perfectly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first rate' reads as one phrase meaning excellent, but 'first' and 'rate for sailors' are separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A tuft or bun of hair worn on the crown of the head is a style of dressing hair.

clue.text: Work at the centre of Paraguayan capital

parts.note: to man is to staff or work a machine or post

indicators.note: at the centre of means only the central four letters of Paraguayan are kept, its outer three each side dropped

explanation.surface: Employment in the middle of the capital of Paraguay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Paraguayan capital' suggests Asunción, but the capital is Nicaragua's; the middle four letters of PARAGUAYAN give AGUA.
explanation.definitionFit: Managua is the capital city of Nicaragua.

clue.text: Short note attached to cheese

parts.note: Brie is a French cheese
F is a musical note

explanation.surface: A little label stuck on a piece of cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: Brief means lasting a short time or using few words.

clue.text: Love son having skill to grab small article

indicators.note: to grab means the son and skill pieces close around the others

parts.note: art means skill
wee is Scots for small
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: A beloved son with the knack for snatching a small item.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to grab' means the son-and-skill pair closes round the other two pieces; WEE is Scots for small.
explanation.definitionFit: A term of endearment for a beloved person, like darling.

clue.text: What's bluff just between Scots river and loch

indicators.note: between means the word for just sits between the river and the loch

parts.note: the Forth is a Scottish river flowing to Edinburgh
right means just or fair
Ness is the famous Scottish loch

explanation.surface: A puzzle about what is fair between a Scottish river and a loch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bluff' is an adjective meaning frank, not a cliff or a bluff in poker.
explanation.definitionFit: Being bluff means being blunt and outspoken; the abstract noun names that plain-spoken quality.

clue.text: Doubter not going all the way in story is understandable

indicators.note: in means the shortened name sits inside the story word

parts.note: a fable is a story

indicators.note: not going all the way means the last letter of the doubter's name is dropped

parts.note: Doubting Thomas, the apostle, is the proverbial doubter

explanation.surface: A sceptic who won't commit appears in a story that makes sense.
explanation.walkthrough: The doubter is Doubting Thomas; 'not going all the way' drops his last letter, and 'in' places what is left inside the story word.
explanation.definitionFit: If something can be fathomed it can be grasped or comprehended.

clue.text: Oil rig mob wrecked in confused situation

indicators.note: wrecked means the letters of oil rig mob are smashed into a new order

explanation.surface: A mob wrecking an oil rig makes a chaotic scene.
explanation.definitionFit: An imbroglio is an entangled, complicated mess or embarrassing muddle.

clue.text: Current uprising is hard and ferocious

indicators.note: uprising, in a down clue, means the word for current is read upwards

parts.note: a flow is a current
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A rising current that is hard and savage, like a revolt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uprising' turns FLOW into WOLF.
explanation.definitionFit: Wolfish describes fierce, predatory behaviour like that of a wolf.

clue.text: Many upset with EEC in the city once

indicators.note: upset means the letters of many and EEC are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: Many in the old city were upset with the European Economic Community.
explanation.walkthrough: The EEC was the forerunner of the EU; here it is just three letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Mycenae was a major Bronze Age Greek city, home of Agamemnon, now ruins.

clue.text: Tailless parasite covering head of tulip plant

indicators.note: covering means the shortened parasite wraps around that letter
tailless means the last letter of the parasite is cut off

parts.note: a louse is a parasitic insect

indicators.note: head of means the first letter of tulip is taken

explanation.surface: A pest with no tail sits on top of a tulip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tailless' cuts LOUSE to LOUS, which goes round T.
explanation.definitionFit: The lotus is a water lily, a plant of the flowering kind.

clue.text: Time to regret being straight

parts.note: to rue is to regret

explanation.surface: A moment to feel sorry about being honest.
explanation.definitionFit: True means straight in the sense of level and accurately aligned.
